title: Pre-Flight Inspection Checklist for FieldHawk Spray Missions
text: Complete the following inspection before every sortie. 1) Confirm all arms are unfolded and each arm lock shows no red indicator band. 2) Inspect every propeller for cracks, chips or loose clamps. 3) Seat the PowerCell until the latch clicks and verify that charge is at least 95% for a full-tank mission. 4) Check that the spray tank cap is closed and nozzles are free of residue. 5) Confirm the HawkOS status LED shows solid green (RTK fixed) or slow green blinking (GNSS lock). 6) Verify that wind is within limits and that no persons are within 6 m of the take-off point. 7) Sign the checklist in AgroSense under Mission > Pre-flight; missions cannot be uploaded to the aircraft until it is signed.

title: Compass Calibration After Magnetic Interference Warning (HK-211)
text: Warning HK-211 indicates that the magnetometer reading deviates from the expected geomagnetic field by more than 15%. Common sources are borewell pump motors, steel water tanks, vehicle bodies, reinforced concrete and buried pipelines. Move at least 10 m away from such objects before calibrating. In AgroSense, open Aircraft > Sensors > Compass Calibration. When the status LED flashes yellow, rotate the aircraft horizontally through 360 degrees until the LED turns solid green, then hold it nose-down and rotate through 360 degrees again. A fast red flash indicates failure; relocate and repeat. Recalibrate whenever the operating site changes by more than 50 km. If HK-211 persists after two successful calibrations, inspect the GNSS mast and its cable for physical damage.

title: Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) Calibration
text: Perform IMU calibration when HawkOS reports HK-214 (IMU bias out of range), after a hard landing or transport shock, or when the ambient temperature differs by more than 20 °C from that of the last calibration. Empty the spray tank and place the aircraft on a flat, rigid surface with less than 2 degrees of tilt; a vehicle bed or soft soil is not acceptable. Allow the aircraft to reach ambient temperature for 10 minutes. Start the procedure from AgroSense > Aircraft > Sensors > IMU Calibration. Do not touch, walk near or move the aircraft during calibration, which takes 5 to 8 minutes; the status LED alternates red and yellow throughout. Any vibration aborts the procedure. Restart the aircraft after completion.

title: Weak GNSS Signal and Insufficient Satellite Count (HK-221)
text: HK-221 is raised when fewer than 12 satellites are tracked or the horizontal dilution of precision (HDOP) exceeds 1.5. In this state the aircraft cannot enter position-hold mode and missions cannot start. After a cold start, or when the aircraft has been moved more than 300 km since its last use, allow 3 to 5 minutes for almanac download with the aircraft stationary. Take off from an open location away from tree canopies, buildings and hillsides that block the southern sky. Keep the GNSS mast on top of the airframe clean and unobstructed; do not place spray hoses, cloth or mobile phones over it. The current satellite count is shown on the HawkRC status bar.

title: RTK Fix Loss During an Active Mission (HK-226)
text: When the RTK solution degrades from FIX to FLOAT or SINGLE during a mission, HawkOS raises HK-226, pauses spraying and holds position. If FIX is not restored within 30 seconds, the aircraft performs the action selected under Mission Settings > RTK Loss Action: Return to Home (default), Hover, or Continue with GNSS (accuracy approximately 1.5 m). Common causes are disturbance of the base station tripod, base battery depletion, obstruction of line of sight between base and aircraft, distance beyond 3 km, or, for network RTK, loss of mobile data on the HawkRC SIM. Once FIX is regained, resume the paused mission from its breakpoint in AgroSense; overlap with the already sprayed area is handled automatically.

title: PinPoint B1 Base Station Setup and Survey-In
text: Erect the tripod on firm ground in an open area with no obstruction above 15 degrees elevation and at least 3 m from vehicles or metal structures. Level the PinPoint B1 using the bubble vial, then hold the power button for 3 seconds. Select Survey-In mode for a new site; the unit averages its position for 5 minutes, during which the status LED blinks blue. For repeat work on the same field, select Known Point to reuse a stored coordinate and eliminate the wait. When the LED turns solid green, corrections are being broadcast on the 865-867 MHz band. Link the aircraft in AgroSense > RTK > Base Station. Effective range is 3 km line of sight, and the internal battery lasts 8 hours.

title: Geofence and Restricted Airspace Blocking (HK-240)
text: HawkOS enforces airspace zones downloaded from the Digital Sky map at each AgroSense synchronisation. In a red zone, for example within 5 km of an airport perimeter or near defence installations, take-off is blocked and HK-240 is displayed. In a yellow zone, take-off requires a valid flight permission artefact uploaded through AgroSense > Compliance. If the aircraft reaches a zone boundary during a mission, it brakes, hovers for 5 seconds and then returns along the flown path. Operator-defined farm geofences behave in the same way, with a 2 m buffer. Zone data older than 30 days triggers a warning; synchronise the app over the internet before travelling to remote fields.

title: Return-to-Home (RTH) Triggers, Altitude and Home Point
text: Return-to-Home is initiated by any of the following: pressing and holding the RTH button on HawkRC for 2 seconds; battery charge falling to the calculated level required to reach home plus a 10% reserve (Smart RTH); RTK loss or signal-loss failsafe, if so configured; or mission completion when 'Return after mission' is enabled. During RTH the aircraft climbs to the RTH altitude (default 20 m, range 5-60 m), flies directly to the home point and descends. The home point is recorded at take-off; update it in AgroSense if the operator relocates. Set the RTH altitude above the tallest obstacle on the return path, such as trees or poles. Press Pause once to cancel RTH.

title: Wind Speed Operating Limits for FieldHawk F2 and F3
text: The FieldHawk F2 is rated for sustained winds up to 6 m/s (21.6 km/h). The FieldHawk F3, owing to its six-rotor configuration and greater mass, is rated up to 8 m/s (28.8 km/h). Gusts must not exceed these values by more than 2 m/s. HawkOS estimates wind speed from attitude data and displays HK-250 (High Wind) when 90% of the limit is reached; spraying continues, but flight speed is reduced by 30%. At 100% of the limit the aircraft stops the mission and holds position awaiting operator action. Halcyon recommends operating below 3 m/s for best spray deposition on either model. Avoid flying between 12:00 and 15:00 in summer, when thermal gusts are strongest.

title: Motor or Electronic Speed Controller Fault (HK-312)
text: HK-312 indicates that an electronic speed controller (ESC) has reported abnormal current, a motor stall, or a motor temperature above 95 °C. The affected motor number (M1-M4 on F2, M1-M6 on F3, counted clockwise from front-right) is shown on HawkRC. Symptoms include a motor that fails to start at arming, spins noticeably slower than the others, or produces a grinding noise. Power off and rotate the motor by hand; resistance or grit indicates bearing contamination from dust or chemical residue. Check the motor connector for corrosion. If the fault moves to another position when the arm cables are swapped, the ESC is defective. Do not fly with an active HK-312; raise a service request with the flight log.

title: Propeller Damage and Excessive Vibration (HK-318)
text: Excessive airframe vibration is reported as HK-318 when measured vibration exceeds 3 g RMS on any axis. The most common cause is propeller damage: cracks, chipped leading edges larger than 2 mm, or warping after storage in direct sunlight. Replace damaged propellers as a matched clockwise and counter-clockwise pair; never repair blades with tape or adhesive. Verify that folding blades open fully and that the propeller clamp bolts are tightened to 1.2 N·m. Unbalanced propellers degrade positioning accuracy, raise motor temperature and can loosen airframe fasteners. After replacement, perform a one-minute hover at 3 m and confirm that the vibration indicator in AgroSense remains green.

title: Obstacle Avoidance Radar Operation and Limitations
text: FieldHawk aircraft carry forward and rearward millimetre-wave radars that detect obstacles between 1.5 m and 30 m. When an obstacle is detected in the direction of travel, the aircraft decelerates, holds position at least 4 m from it and displays 'Obstacle Ahead' on HawkRC; the operator must then steer around it manually or edit the route. The radar cannot reliably detect thin wires, guy ropes or bare branches under 2 cm in diameter. Clean the radome with a damp cloth at the end of each day, as pesticide residue and mud reduce detection range. HK-410 indicates a radar self-test failure; avoidance is then disabled and mission speed is limited to 3 m/s.

title: Terrain-Follow Radar and Height Above Crop Canopy
text: The downward-facing terrain radar maintains a set height of 1.5 to 5 m above the crop canopy and compensates for slopes up to 15 degrees. On terraced or steeper land, plan the mission in AgroSense using 3D Terrain mode instead. Over standing water, such as flooded paddy, the radar may read the water surface and cause the aircraft to descend below the target height; increase the set height by 1 m. Sparse or newly sown crops can cause height fluctuation as the radar alternates between canopy and bare soil. HK-415 indicates degraded terrain radar returns; the aircraft then climbs to 6 m and switches to barometric altitude for the rest of the mission.

title: Pairing HawkRC with an Aircraft
text: Pairing is required when a new or replacement HawkRC is used, after a controller factory reset, or after the aircraft flight controller has been replaced. Power on both devices within 2 m of each other. On HawkRC, open Settings > Link > Pair Aircraft. Within 60 seconds, press and hold the link button beside the aircraft battery bay for 3 seconds until the status LED flashes purple. Successful pairing is confirmed by a solid green link icon on HawkRC and a tone from the aircraft. HK-501 (Link Timeout) indicates that the pairing window expired; repeat the procedure. One HawkRC can store up to five aircraft profiles, selectable under Settings > Link > Aircraft List.

title: Remote Controller Signal Loss Failsafe
text: If the HawkRC control link is lost for more than 3 seconds, HawkOS executes the configured failsafe action: Return to Home (default), Hover, or Land. A mission in progress continues autonomously to the end of the current spray line before the failsafe executes. Typical range is 2 km in open terrain; range drops sharply behind trees, sugarcane or buildings, or when the operator stands in a ditch. Keep both HawkRC antennas parallel and pointing upward, with their flat faces toward the aircraft. When the link is restored, a tone sounds, and manual control resumes once the operator moves either stick. Configure the failsafe action under HawkRC Settings > Safety > Signal Loss.

title: Exporting Flight Logs for Analysis and Support
text: HawkOS records a binary flight log (.hlog) for every power cycle and stores the most recent 200 flights in internal memory, overwriting the oldest. To export, connect the aircraft to the AgroSense app with internet access, open Fleet > Aircraft > Flight Records, select the flights and tap Upload; uploaded logs remain available on the web portal for one year. Without connectivity, connect a laptop to the USB-C port beneath the GNSS mast, power on the aircraft and copy files from the HAWKLOG folder. Halcyon support requires the relevant .hlog file for any crash or warranty investigation. Do not rename or edit log files, because altered checksums cause the files to be rejected.

title: Horizontal Drift During Hover
text: If the aircraft drifts more than 1.5 m within 10 seconds while hovering in calm air with the sticks released, first check the flight mode shown on HawkRC. ATTI mode, entered automatically when GNSS positioning is lost, does not hold position and requires continuous manual correction. If the mode is P-GNSS or P-RTK, the HawkRC sticks may not be returning to centre; open Settings > Sticks and confirm that centred output is within 3%, recalibrating if necessary. A partially filled tank can cause slow fore-aft oscillation as liquid sloshes, so the anti-slosh baffle must be installed. A widening circular drift indicates a compass fault; follow the compass calibration procedure.

title: Altitude Hold Instability and Barometer Faults (HK-233)
text: In position-hold flight the aircraft should maintain altitude within 0.3 m with RTK, or within 1 m without RTK. A gradual climb or descent with the throttle stick centred usually results from barometer disturbance. Verify that the foam cover over the barometer port, located under the top shell, is present and dry; spray mist or rainwater ingress causes erratic readings. A rapid temperature change, such as moving the aircraft from an air-conditioned vehicle into 40 °C sunlight, causes altitude drift for the first 5 minutes, so allow it to acclimatise. HK-233 indicates a disagreement exceeding 2 m between barometric and RTK altitude. If HK-233 persists after drying, replace the barometer foam (part FH-BF-02) through PartsDesk.

title: Emergency Motor Stop Procedure
text: The emergency motor stop immediately cuts power to all motors and must be used only to prevent injury, for example when a person or animal is about to be struck or the aircraft is entangled. In flight, the aircraft will fall. To execute, pull both HawkRC sticks to the bottom inner corners (left stick down-right, right stick down-left) and hold for 2 seconds. In flight, this combination is active only when 'Emergency Stop in Flight' is enabled under HawkRC Settings > Safety; on the ground it is always active. To stop motors normally after landing, hold the left stick fully down for 3 seconds. Each emergency stop is logged as event E-STOP and requires a full pre-flight inspection before re-arming.

title: Arming Refused: Common Causes and Resolution
text: When the aircraft refuses to arm, HawkRC displays the blocking condition on its main screen. The most frequent conditions are: IMU warming, which below 10 °C ambient can take up to 3 minutes; compass error HK-211; fewer than 12 satellites (HK-221) in P-GNSS mode; battery charge below 30% or cell voltage difference above 0.1 V; aircraft tilted more than 10 degrees on uneven ground; restricted zone HK-240; unsigned pre-flight checklist; and firmware mismatch between HawkOS and the PowerCell, shown as HK-120. Resolve the listed condition and retry. Arming is also blocked for 10 seconds after an emergency stop. If no reason is displayed, restart both the aircraft and HawkRC.

title: HawkOS Status LED Colour Codes
text: The status LED on the aircraft's rear arm indicates system state as follows. Solid green: RTK FIX, ready to fly. Slow green blink: GNSS lock without RTK. Fast yellow blink: compass calibration required. Alternating red and yellow: IMU warming or calibrating. Slow red blink: low battery, below 30%. Fast red blink: critical battery or sensor error; land immediately. Solid red: hardware fault; do not fly. Solid blue: firmware update in progress; do not power off. Purple flash: pairing mode. The front arm LEDs are navigation lights, showing red on the left and green on the right in normal flight; they flash white while Return-to-Home is active.

title: Operating Near High-Tension Power Lines
text: Maintain a minimum horizontal separation of 15 m from distribution lines up to 33 kV and 30 m from transmission lines of 66 kV and above. Never fly beneath conductors. The obstacle radar cannot reliably detect conductors, and the electromagnetic field near high-voltage lines can induce compass errors and erratic heading. Before planning, mark the line corridor as a no-fly polygon in AgroSense > Field > Obstacles; the mission planner then routes spray lines around it with the required buffer. A field bisected by a transmission line should be split into two separate missions. If heading becomes unstable near a line, switch to manual control and fly away perpendicular to the line.

title: Landing Site Selection and Landing in Tall Crops
text: Avoid landing in standing crops taller than 1 m, such as sugarcane, maize or cotton. Rotor downwash flattens plants, foliage can strike the propellers, and the landing protection radar may detect an uneven surface and refuse to descend, holding at 2 m. Before each mission, set the home point on a clear bund, road or portable landing pad of at least 2 m by 2 m, and confirm it in AgroSense. If a forced landing in crop is unavoidable, descend at no more than 1 m/s and stop the motors as soon as the landing gear touches the ground. Retrieve the aircraft by lifting it vertically; dragging it through stalks damages nozzles and arms.

title: Cleaning a Clogged Spray Nozzle
text: A partially clogged nozzle produces a narrow, uneven jet or intermittent dripping, leaving untreated strips across the field. HawkOS raises warning SP-106 (Flow Deviation) when measured flow differs from the commanded rate by more than 15%. To clean, power off the aircraft and drain the tank. Remove the nozzle tip by turning it a quarter-turn anticlockwise and withdraw the 80-mesh nozzle strainer behind it. Soak both parts in warm water with a neutral detergent for 10 minutes, then scrub with a soft nylon brush. Never insert pins, wires or needles into the orifice, as this permanently deforms the spray pattern. Blow through the tip from the outlet side, reinstall it, and run a 30-second water test to confirm a uniform fan before resuming operation.

title: Selecting a Nozzle Type: Flat-Fan versus Centrifugal
text: The FieldHawk F2 ships with four flat-fan nozzles (110-02 tips); the FieldHawk F3 ships with two centrifugal atomising nozzles. Both aircraft accept either kit. Flat-fan nozzles produce coarse droplets of 250–400 µm, resist drift and are recommended for herbicides and contact products applied at 15–25 L/ha. Centrifugal nozzles use a motor-driven disc to produce adjustable droplets of 80–300 µm, giving better penetration and leaf-underside coverage in dense canopies such as sugarcane, cotton and orchards; they are recommended for insecticides and fungicides at low volumes of 8–15 L/ha. After changing the kit, select the matching nozzle profile under AgroSense > Aircraft > Spray System, because an incorrect profile causes inaccurate application rates. Recalibrate flow after every nozzle change.

title: Flow-Rate Calibration Procedure
text: Flow calibration aligns the commanded application rate with actual delivery. Perform it after changing nozzles or chemical formulation, whenever the applied volume differs from the planned volume by more than 5%, and every 50 flight hours. Place the aircraft on level ground, fill the tank with exactly 5 L of clean water and open AgroSense > Spray > Flow Calibration. Tap Start; the pump runs at a fixed 2.0 L/min for 60 seconds. Collect the output in a graduated container, or measure the volume remaining in the tank, and enter the actual volume dispensed. AgroSense calculates a new flowmeter K-factor and uploads it to HawkOS. Repeat the test; the calibration is accepted when two consecutive runs agree within ±3%.

title: Pump Fails to Prime After the Tank Runs Dry (Air Lock)
text: If the tank is run empty or the inlet hose is disconnected, air enters the pump chamber and the diaphragm pump cannot draw liquid. The pump motor remains audible but no liquid reaches the nozzles; HawkOS reports SP-101 (Pump Running, No Flow) after 8 seconds. To prime, add at least 3 L of liquid to the tank and confirm that the inlet filter is seated. Open the bleed screw on the pump head one full turn. On HawkRC, open Spray > Manual and hold the Prime button for 10 seconds until a steady, bubble-free stream exits the bleed port, then close the screw. Check all inlet hose clamps for air ingress. Do not run the pump dry for more than 30 seconds, as this damages the diaphragm.

title: Inaccurate Tank Level Sensor Readings
text: The spray tank uses a pressure-based level sensor mounted at the tank base. Readings become inaccurate if the aircraft is not level during filling, if chemical residue blocks the sensor port, or if the mixture density differs from water by more than 10%, as with concentrated liquid fertiliser. Symptoms include an incorrect remaining-volume display on HawkRC or a premature 'Tank Empty' return-to-home. To recalibrate, rinse the sensor port, place the aircraft on level ground, empty the tank completely and select AgroSense > Spray > Tank Sensor > Set Zero. Then fill to the 10 L (F2) or 16 L (F3) mark and select Set Full. For dense mixtures, enter the specific gravity in the same menu so that HawkOS can correct the displayed volume.

title: Reducing Spray Drift
text: Spray drift can damage neighbouring crops and contaminate water sources. Halcyon recommends spraying only when wind speed is below 3 m/s; HawkOS blocks automatic missions above 6 m/s. Fly 2–3 m above the canopy, since each additional metre of height substantially increases drift, and limit ground speed to 5 m/s when applying herbicides. Avoid spraying when air temperature exceeds 32 °C or relative humidity falls below 40%, typically between 11:00 and 16:00, because small droplets evaporate and remain airborne. Maintain an untreated buffer of at least 5 m from field edges adjoining sensitive crops and 10 m from ponds, canals and wells; buffers can be drawn as exclusion zones in AgroSense. Using coarser droplets further reduces drift.

title: Adjusting Droplet Size on Centrifugal Nozzles
text: On centrifugal nozzles, droplet size is controlled by disc rotation speed: a higher speed produces finer droplets. Approximate volume median diameters are 90 µm at 12,000 rpm, 150 µm at 9,000 rpm, 250 µm at 6,000 rpm and 350 µm at 4,000 rpm. AgroSense provides three presets under Spray > Droplet Size: Fine (150 µm) for insecticides, Medium (250 µm) for fungicides and Coarse (350 µm) for plant-growth regulators and herbicides. Custom speeds between 4,000 and 12,000 rpm can be entered in steps of 500 rpm. Fine droplets give superior coverage but evaporate and drift more readily, so select Fine only under low-wind conditions. Droplet size settings have no effect when flat-fan nozzles are installed.

title: Chemical Mixing Order and Viscosity Limits
text: The spray system is designed for liquids with a viscosity not exceeding 30 mPa·s. Thicker mixtures overload the pump, reduce flow and trigger SP-106. Wettable powders and water-dispersible granules must be pre-mixed into a slurry in a separate bucket at roughly 1 part product to 5 parts water, then poured through a 100-mesh strainer into a tank already half filled with water. When combining products, add them in this order: wettable powders and granules, suspension concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates, soluble liquids, and finally adjuvants. Top up with water and agitate. Powders settle quickly, so spray the mixture within 2 hours of preparation and re-agitate it if it has stood for more than 15 minutes.

title: Installing and Calibrating the GS-20 Granule Spreader
text: The GS-20 granule spreader converts the FieldHawk F3 into a broadcaster for fertiliser, seed and granular pesticides; it is not compatible with the F2. Capacity is 20 kg. Suitable material is dry and free-flowing with a granule size of 0.5–5 mm, such as urea, DAP or paddy seed. To install, remove the spray tank, mount the spreader on the payload rails and connect it to the payload port; HawkOS detects the attachment automatically. Before the first job, run AgroSense > Spreader > Calibrate with 5 kg of the actual material to determine discharge rate against gate opening. Damp or caked material causes bridging over the gate, so store fertiliser dry and break up lumps before loading. Powdered products are not supported.

title: Post-Spray Rinsing and Cleaning Procedure
text: Chemical residue left in the spray system crystallises, corrodes fittings and contaminates subsequent applications. Clean the system at the end of every working day and before switching between chemical classes, particularly from a herbicide to any other product. Never leave mixture in the tank overnight. Triple-rinse by adding 2 L of clean water, spraying it out over the treated field, and repeating three times. Then circulate 2 L of tank cleaner or 0.5% washing soda solution. Remove and wash the tank filter, nozzle strainers and tips. Wipe the airframe with a damp cloth; do not use pressure washers or direct hose jets on motors and electronics. Dispose of rinse water on the treated area, never into drains, ponds or canals.

title: Leaks at the Tank Seal or Quick-Connect Fitting
text: Leaks usually originate at the tank cap O-ring or at the quick-connect fitting between the tank outlet and the pump inlet. Solvent-based emulsifiable concentrates cause standard nitrile O-rings to swell or crack over time. Leaking liquid can reach the battery compartment and must be corrected before flight. Inspect both O-rings for swelling, cuts or flattening and replace them with the chemical-resistant FKM seal kit (PartsDesk part HX-SK-12). Apply a thin film of silicone grease, reseat the tank, and push the quick-connect until it clicks and the red locking collar is fully hidden. To verify the repair, fill the tank with 5 L of water, run the pump at 50% for 2 minutes, and confirm that no droplets form beneath the tank.

title: Flowmeter Signal Error SP-104
text: Each spray line contains a turbine flowmeter that reports delivered volume to HawkOS. Error SP-104 (Flowmeter Signal Lost) occurs when the pump is commanded on but no flowmeter pulses are received for 5 seconds; spraying is then suspended and the remaining-volume display freezes. Liquid may continue to discharge briefly while the display reads 0 L/min. Common causes are residue jamming the turbine rotor and a loose or corroded 3-pin flowmeter connector. Power off the aircraft, disconnect and inspect the connector, and clean the pins with contact cleaner. Unscrew the flowmeter housing, rinse the rotor in clean water and confirm that it spins freely when blown gently. If SP-104 persists after cleaning, replace the flowmeter assembly through PartsDesk.

title: Recommended Storage Voltage for Long-Term Battery Storage
text: PowerCell batteries degrade rapidly when stored fully charged or deeply discharged. For storage longer than 10 days, keep each cell at 3.80–3.85 V, approximately 40–60% charge. PowerCell packs enter self-discharge mode automatically after 5 days without use and discharge themselves to storage voltage; slight warmth during this period is normal. Alternatively, place the packs in ChargeHub 4 and select Storage mode, which charges or discharges them to storage voltage. Store batteries in a dry, fire-resistant location at 15–25 °C, away from direct sunlight. Check the voltage every 60 days and restore the storage level if any cell falls below 3.70 V. Batteries left below 3.0 V per cell may be permanently locked and require service.

title: Handling a Swollen Battery
text: Swelling indicates gas formation inside one or more cells as a result of over-discharge, physical impact, overheating or age. A pack is considered swollen if the casing bulges, its thickness has increased by more than 2 mm, or it no longer slides into the aircraft or charger without force. Stop using the battery immediately: do not fly, charge or puncture it. Disconnect it and move it outdoors, away from flammable material, into a metal container or a bucket of dry sand. Keep it there for at least 24 hours and observe it for heat or smoke. Then raise a Halcyon Care RMA through AgroSense for collection and safe disposal. Never ship a swollen battery by courier.

title: Cell Imbalance Warning BT-221
text: Each PowerCell contains 14 series cells monitored by the battery management system. Warning BT-221 (Cell Imbalance) is issued when the difference between the highest and lowest cell voltages exceeds 0.10 V. Individual cell voltages can be viewed in AgroSense > Batteries > Cell Details, where out-of-range cells are highlighted in red. Imbalance reduces usable capacity and can cause sudden voltage sag in flight. To correct it, insert the pack in ChargeHub 4, hold the bay button for 3 seconds to start a Balance Charge, and allow it to complete, which can take up to 2 hours. If the deviation remains above 0.15 V after two balance charges, retire the pack from flight use and contact Halcyon service.

title: Battery Too Hot to Charge (Charge Temperature High)
text: PowerCell batteries accept charge only when cell temperature is between 10 °C and 45 °C. Immediately after a spray flight, cell temperature typically reaches 50–60 °C. If a hot pack is inserted, ChargeHub 4 holds the bay in a waiting state and AgroSense shows BT-201 (Charge Temperature High); charging starts automatically once the pack cools below 45 °C. Allow 20–30 minutes in shade with good airflow; the ChargeHub 4 fans also cool packs left in the bays. Never cool batteries with water, ice or a wet cloth, or place them in a refrigerator, because condensation and thermal shock damage the cells. In hot conditions, rotate at least three packs per aircraft so that each has time to cool before charging.

title: Normal Battery Charging Times
text: Charging time depends on the selected mode and the starting state of charge. From 20% to 95% in Fast mode, a PowerCell 22 takes approximately 12 minutes and a PowerCell 30 approximately 15 minutes. Standard mode, which extends battery life, takes about 30 and 40 minutes respectively. Charging from 95% to 100% adds roughly 8 minutes because the charger tapers the current. Times increase when two or more bays charge simultaneously, when the input supply is below 220 V, or when packs must first cool down. A typical spray flight consumes one pack in 9–14 minutes, so Halcyon recommends three to four packs per aircraft for continuous operation with Fast charging.

title: ChargeHub 4 Status LED Meanings
text: Each ChargeHub 4 bay has a status LED. Pulsing green: charging. Solid green: fully charged. Solid blue: Storage mode in progress or complete. Slow yellow blink: waiting, usually because the pack is outside the 10–45 °C charging range. Solid red: battery fault, such as BT-221 imbalance or an authentication failure; check AgroSense for details. Fast red blink on all bays: charger over-temperature or cooling fan failure; disconnect power, clear the vents and allow 15 minutes to cool. Alternating red and yellow on all bays: input voltage outside 190–260 V or frequency outside 47–53 Hz. If a fault persists after restarting the hub, note the LED pattern and contact Halcyon service.

title: Generator Sizing for Field Charging
text: ChargeHub 4 draws up to 7.0 kW in Fast mode from a single-phase 220–240 V, 50 Hz supply. For full-rate Fast charging, use a generator rated at least 9 kVA continuous. With a 5–8 kVA generator, enable Eco mode in the hub settings, which limits draw to 3.5 kW and roughly doubles charging time. Generators below 5 kVA are not supported and will trip or cause input faults. Use generators with automatic voltage regulation or inverter technology; do not supply the hub from modified-sine-wave inverters or tractor-mounted converters. Connect the hub directly, without extension cables longer than 10 m, ensure that the generator is earthed, and place it at least 5 m downwind of the charging area.

title: Battery Cycle Count and End-of-Life Criteria
text: PowerCell batteries are rated for 1,000 charge cycles while retaining at least 80% of their original capacity under recommended use. Cycle count and State of Health (SoH) are displayed in AgroSense > Batteries. As capacity declines, flight time per pack shortens. HawkOS issues advisory BT-240 when SoH falls below 75% or the count exceeds 1,000 cycles. Takeoff is blocked with BT-245 when SoH falls below 65% or the count exceeds 1,500 cycles, because aged packs may sag under full spray loads. Retired packs must not be discarded with household waste. Discharge them to below 30%, then return them to any Halcyon service centre, which arranges recycling through an authorised e-waste partner.

title: Transporting Batteries by Road
text: Lithium-polymer packs must be transported at reduced charge. Before travelling, discharge each PowerCell to 30–50% using Storage mode on ChargeHub 4. Fit the supplied terminal caps and place each pack in its individual protective case or a fire-resistant battery box, packed so that batteries cannot move or strike one another. In cars and pickups, carry batteries in the load area; never carry them in the passenger cabin of buses or other shared vehicles. Do not leave batteries in a closed vehicle parked in sunlight, as interior temperatures can exceed 60 °C. On two-wheelers, carry no more than one pack, in a hard case secured to the carrier. Swollen or damaged packs must not be transported.

title: Battery Behaviour in Cold Weather
text: At low temperatures the internal resistance of lithium-polymer cells rises, reducing available capacity and causing voltage sag under load. Below 15 °C, flight time may fall by up to 20%. HawkOS displays BT-212 (Battery Temperature Low) and prevents takeoff if cell temperature is below 10 °C. Keep packs indoors or in an insulated box overnight and pre-warm them to at least 20 °C before flight; ChargeHub 4 Warm mode heats packs in the bays to 25 °C in about 10 minutes. After takeoff, hover for 30 seconds at low height to confirm stable voltage. Charging is held below 10 °C, so let cold packs reach room temperature first. Raise the low-battery return threshold by 5% in winter.

title: Battery Not Recognised: Cleaning Corroded Contacts
text: A PowerCell that is not detected by the aircraft or by a ChargeHub 4 bay, or that intermittently triggers BT-230 (Battery Communication Lost), most often has contaminated or corroded contacts. Pesticide and fertiliser residue produces green, white or black deposits on the main power terminals and on the two small communication pins. Power off the aircraft and remove the battery, then inspect both the battery contacts and the matching aircraft or charger contacts. Clean them with isopropyl alcohol (90% or higher) and a soft brass brush or cotton swab; do not use sandpaper, files or water. Allow 5 minutes to dry before reinserting. Bent communication pins or pitted contacts must be replaced through PartsDesk or a service centre.

title: Initial Commissioning and Row-Width Configuration of Tiller-X
text: Before first use, charge the TX-Pack to 100% on the charging dock and pair Tiller-X with the AgroSense app by scanning the QR code on the rear service panel. Under Settings > Field Profile, enter the crop row spacing (supported range 30–120 cm) and the number of rows covered per pass. The wheel track must then be set mechanically: loosen the four axle clamp bolts, slide each wheel hub to the marked position (1.0–1.6 m, in 10 cm increments) and re-torque the bolts to 85 Nm. The wheel track must be an exact multiple of the row spacing; otherwise AgroSense displays warning TX-W012 'Track/row mismatch' and blocks mission start. Complete a 10 m supervised test run at 1 km/h before the first autonomous mission.

title: Calibrating Row-Following Guidance on Tiller-X
text: Tiller-X follows crop rows primarily with its stereo camera, using RTK positioning as a secondary reference. Recalibrate row guidance if the robot drifts laterally, weaves between rows, or AgroSense reports a tracking error greater than 5 cm. Select a straight row section at least 20 m long with crop height above 8 cm. In AgroSense, open Tiller-X > Tools > Row Guidance Calibration, position the robot centred over the row, and tap Start. The robot drives 20 m forward at 0.8 km/h and then reverses to the start point. Calibration passes when the residual error is below 2 cm. Repeat the calibration after changing crop type, after the camera has been removed or refitted, or if the camera bracket has been struck.

title: Resolving Front LiDAR Obstruction Faults (TX-E204)
text: The front LiDAR detects obstacles up to 25 m ahead of the robot. When more than 30% of its optical window is blocked by mud, dust or crop residue, TX-Drive raises fault TX-E204 'LiDAR view obstructed', stops the robot and flashes the status light amber. To clear the fault, apply the parking brake from the app, switch off the main power isolator, and clean the window with clean water and a soft microfibre cloth. Do not use pressure washers, solvents or abrasive pads, which damage the anti-reflective coating. Power on and run Sensor Check in AgroSense. In dusty conditions, enable Auto-Purge, which directs compressed air across the window every 15 minutes. Persistent TX-E204 on a clean window indicates a coating defect requiring service.

title: Stereo Camera Performance Under Low Sun Angles
text: When the sun is less than 15° above the horizon and ahead of the robot, direct glare can saturate the stereo camera. TX-Drive then reports warning TX-W215 'Vision confidence low', reduces speed to 1 km/h and, if confidence remains below 40% for 10 seconds, pauses the mission. Recommended actions: schedule missions to avoid the first hour after sunrise and the last hour before sunset; where the field layout permits, orient rows so the robot travels perpendicular to the sun; fit the optional SH-2 camera sun hood; and keep the lens covers free of smudges. Enable RTK-Assist in Mission Settings so that guidance can continue from positioning data during brief glare events.

title: Safety Bumper Activation and Reset Procedure
text: The front and rear safety bumpers contain pressure-sensitive edges. A contact force above 50 N stops all drive motors and the implement within 0.3 seconds and raises fault TX-E101 'Bumper contact'; the status light turns solid red. Before resetting, inspect the surroundings for people, animals or obstructions and remove the cause. Then press and hold the yellow Resume button on the rear panel for 3 seconds, or confirm Resume in AgroSense. If TX-E101 recurs without any contact, check the bumper for cracks or soil packed behind the sensing edge, and verify that the bumper connector is fully seated. A bumper that does not return to its rest position must be replaced before further operation.

title: Pairing and Using the Tiller-X Kill-Switch Fob
text: Each Tiller-X is supplied with a handheld kill-switch fob that maintains a continuous radio link with the robot, with a range of up to 150 m line of sight. Pressing the red button triggers an immediate safety stop. If the robot receives no fob heartbeat for 1 second, it stops and reports TX-E120 'Fob link lost'. To pair a new or replacement fob, power on the robot and hold the pairing button inside the rear service panel for 5 seconds until the status light blinks blue, then hold the fob's red and green buttons together for 3 seconds. A solid green fob LED confirms pairing. Only one fob can be paired at a time. Replace the fob's CR2032 cell when its LED blinks red.

title: Diagnosing Low Hydraulic Pressure (TX-E310)
text: The hydraulic implement lift operates at a nominal pressure of 120 bar. If pressure falls below 85 bar during a lift command, TX-Drive raises fault TX-E310 'Hydraulic pressure low', and the implement may fail to rise or may sink slowly under load. With the implement fully lowered, check the reservoir sight glass; the oil level must lie between the MIN and MAX marks. Top up only with ISO VG 46 hydraulic oil. Inspect hoses and quick couplers for leaks or air ingress, and confirm that the couplers are fully engaged. A clogged suction strainer also reduces pressure and should be cleaned. If pressure remains low after these checks, the pump requires inspection at a Halcyon service centre.

title: Hydraulic Oil Overtemperature Warnings (TX-W320 / TX-E321)
text: Hydraulic oil temperature is monitored at the reservoir. At 75 °C, TX-Drive issues warning TX-W320 and reduces the implement cycling rate; at 85 °C, it raises fault TX-E321, lowers the implement and stops the mission. Common causes are continuous lift-and-lower cycles on short rows, ambient temperatures above 40 °C, a blocked oil cooler fin pack, and incorrect oil grade. Allow the system to cool with the robot parked in shade for at least 30 minutes, and do not open the reservoir cap while the oil is hot. Clean the oil cooler fins with low-pressure air, blowing from the inside outward. Use only ISO VG 46 oil; a lower-viscosity grade thins excessively at temperature and accelerates overheating.

title: Mounting the Weeder-W Inter-Row Weeding Attachment
text: Park Tiller-X on level ground and lower the implement lift fully. Align the Weeder-W frame behind the rear quick-coupler and reverse the robot slowly using the jog control in AgroSense until the coupler hooks engage. Switch off the main power isolator, insert both locking pins and secure each with its R-clip. Connect the two hydraulic hoses, matching red to red and blue to blue, and then the 8-pin implement connector. On power-up, TX-Drive reads the attachment's ID chip; if Weeder-W is not recognised within 10 seconds, fault TX-E330 'Implement not detected' is displayed, in which case clean the connector pins and reconnect. Finally, set the tine working width in AgroSense to the inter-row gap minus 10 cm.

title: Adjusting Working Depth of the Ridger-R Attachment
text: Ridger-R forms ridges with a working depth adjustable from 5 to 20 cm. Coarse depth is set mechanically by moving the depth-wheel pin between the six holes on each side bracket; each hole changes depth by approximately 3 cm, and both sides must use the same hole. Fine depth is set in AgroSense under Implement > Ridger-R > Target Depth, where the hydraulic lift holds the selected depth within ±1 cm. If ridge height is uneven, verify that both depth-wheel tyres are inflated to 1.2 bar and that the side brackets are level. In heavy clay or dry, compacted soil, reduce depth by 3–5 cm and complete the ridge in two passes to avoid overloading the drive motors.

title: Recovering Tiller-X from Wheel Slip in Waterlogged Soil
text: TX-Drive continuously compares wheel speed with RTK ground speed. If slip exceeds 40% for more than 5 seconds, the robot stops and reports TX-E420 'Traction lost' to prevent rutting and motor damage. Do not repeatedly retry forward motion. Raise the implement fully, then select Recovery Mode in AgroSense, which applies low-torque alternating forward and reverse pulses for up to 60 seconds. If the robot remains immobile, attach a tow strap to the front recovery eyes only, never to the bumper or implement frame, and pull straight back along the robot's own track. Avoid operating in saturated fields; wait until soil from the top 10 cm no longer forms a ribbon when squeezed by hand.

title: Slope and Side-Tilt Operating Limits
text: Tiller-X is rated for operation on longitudinal slopes up to 15° (27%) and side slopes up to 10° (18%). An onboard inclinometer monitors pitch and roll continuously. At 8° of roll, TX-Drive issues warning TX-W410 and reduces speed to 1 km/h; at 10° of roll or 15° of pitch, it stops the robot, raises fault TX-E411 'Tilt limit exceeded' and lowers the implement to stabilise the chassis. On terraced or sloping fields, plan rows to run up and down the slope rather than across it. Mounted implements raise the centre of gravity; with Ridger-R fitted, set the side-slope limit to 7° in AgroSense. Tilt faults must never be manually overridden.

title: Replacing the TX-Pack Battery Module
text: The TX-Pack is a 48 V, 2.4 kWh lithium-ion module providing approximately 5 hours of weeding operation. It is not hot-swappable. To replace it, move the robot to level ground, pause or end the mission, and turn the main power isolator to OFF. Release the two latches on the battery bay cover, pull the red handle to disengage the power connector, and slide the pack out using both carrying handles (pack mass 18 kg). Insert the charged pack until the connector clicks, close the latches and switch on. The five-segment gauge on the pack shows its charge level, and a paused mission resumes from the last recorded position. Packs below 10% charge should not be stored for longer than 7 days.

title: Troubleshooting Charging Dock Docking Failures (TX-E610)
text: Tiller-X returns to its charging dock automatically on mission completion or when the TX-Pack falls to 15%. It aligns using the infrared beacon on the dock mast and must meet the two spring-loaded charging plates within ±3 cm. After three unsuccessful attempts, the robot stops 2 m in front of the dock and reports TX-E610 'Docking failed'. Check that the dock stands on firm, level ground with a clear 3 m approach path, that the beacon window is clean and its LED is steady green, and that the charging plates are free of mud and corrosion. If the dock has been relocated, re-register its position in AgroSense under Fleet > Dock > Set Location.

title: Eliminating Missed Strips in Tiller-X Coverage Paths
text: Untreated strips between passes usually result from insufficient pass overlap, degraded positioning, or a field boundary drawn inside the cropped area. Pass width equals rows per pass multiplied by row spacing; set overlap to at least 5 cm in Mission Settings. If the PinPoint B1 base station loses RTK fix, Tiller-X falls back to float mode with approximately ±30 cm accuracy and AgroSense logs TX-W705 'RTK float'; ensure the base station has an unobstructed sky view and is within 5 km. Review the coverage map after each mission, where grey strips indicate unworked areas. Use Mission > Fill Gaps to generate a supplementary path that covers only the missed areas.

title: Resolving Headland Turn Failures
text: At each row end, Tiller-X performs a programmed headland turn with a minimum turning radius of 2.5 m. The headland, the uncropped strip at the field edge, must be at least 4 m wide for a U-turn, or 6 m wide when Ridger-R is fitted and a three-point turn is required. If the turn path would cross the field boundary or an obstacle is detected, the robot aborts the turn and reports TX-E450 'Headland turn aborted'. Redraw the field boundary in AgroSense so that it encloses the full headland, not only the cropped area. Confirm that Lift-at-Headland is enabled so the implement rises at the row end. On soft headlands, select Wide Turn mode to reduce wheel scrubbing.

title: Drive Motor Thermal Derating
text: Each of the four in-hub drive motors contains a winding temperature sensor. At 90 °C, TX-Drive reports warning TX-W510 'Motor derating' and limits maximum speed and torque to 50% of rated values; at 110 °C, it raises fault TX-E512 and stops the robot until the winding cools below 70 °C, which typically takes 20–30 minutes. Derating commonly occurs with deep working depth in heavy soil, continuous operation above 40 °C ambient, or dried mud packed around the motor cooling fins. Clean the hub fins after every working day, and reduce working depth or speed when warnings recur. A single motor that overheats while the others remain cool may indicate a dragging brake or failed bearing requiring service.

title: Adjusting Rubber Track Tension on the Tiller-X Track Kit
text: The optional Track Kit replaces the wheels with rubber tracks for wet or soft soils. Correct tension gives a sag of 15–20 mm, measured midway between the drive sprocket and the idler with the robot on level ground. Excessive sag allows the track to ride over the sprocket teeth, producing a clicking noise and possible derailment; over-tensioning increases rolling resistance and bearing wear. To adjust, loosen the idler lock nut, turn the tensioner bolt clockwise to tighten or anticlockwise to slacken, and re-torque the lock nut to 60 Nm. Remove packed mud before measuring. Check tension after the first 10 operating hours and every 50 hours thereafter.

title: Operating Tiller-X in Rain and Wet Conditions
text: Tiller-X electronics are rated IP65 and the drive motors IP67, permitting operation in light rain of up to 10 mm per hour. Suspend operation in heavy rain or thunderstorms, or where standing water exceeds 15 cm in depth. TX-Drive pauses the mission automatically if the onboard rain sensor detects sustained heavy rainfall for 5 minutes; this is normal behaviour, not a fault. Never open the battery bay or service panels while the robot is wet, and do not send the robot to the charging dock until the charging plates are dry. Wipe water droplets from the LiDAR window and camera lenses before resuming. After rain, allow the soil to drain to avoid traction loss and compaction.

title: Free-Wheel Mode for Towing and Transport
text: If Tiller-X must be moved without power, for example after a TX-Pack failure, engage free-wheel mode. Switch off the main power isolator, then rotate the brake-release lever on each of the four wheel hubs a quarter turn to the FREE position, which disengages the motor holding brakes. The robot can then be pushed, or towed from the front recovery eyes at no more than 5 km/h. For transport between fields, load the robot onto a trailer using ramps rated for at least 500 kg, return all four levers to LOCK, and secure the chassis at the four marked tie-down points. Never tow the robot with free-wheel engaged on public roads or down slopes.

title: Updating TX-Drive Firmware via AgroSense
text: TX-Drive firmware updates are delivered over the air through AgroSense. When an update is available, a notification appears under Fleet > Tiller-X > Firmware. Before installing, ensure that the robot is docked or the TX-Pack is above 50%, that it is connected to Wi-Fi or 4G with a stable signal, and that no mission is active. Installation takes approximately 20 minutes; the status light blinks purple throughout and the robot may restart twice. Do not switch off power or move the robot during this period. If installation is interrupted, the robot reverts to the previous version and reports TX-E720 'Update failed'; retry once connectivity is restored. Recalibrate row guidance after any major version update.

title: 250-Hour Scheduled Maintenance
text: Perform the following tasks every 250 operating hours or annually, whichever occurs first. Replace the hydraulic return filter and clean the suction strainer; check the oil level, and replace the oil every 1,000 hours. Check the wheel hub bolts and torque them to 85 Nm. Inspect the safety bumper edges and perform a bumper function test, then test the kill-switch fob stop. Clean the LiDAR window and camera lenses and inspect them for scratches. Lubricate the quick-coupler pivots and lift-arm grease nipples with lithium grease. Inspect the TX-Pack connector pins for discolouration. AgroSense displays reminder TX-I250 at 240 hours; record completion in Fleet > Maintenance Log. Service kit TXK-250 is available through PartsDesk.

title: Correcting Row Offset to Prevent Crop Damage
text: If Weeder-W tines or the robot's wheels cut, crush or uproot crop plants consistently on one side, the lateral row offset is likely incorrect. The row offset defines the distance between the robot centreline and the crop row centre; an error of more than 3 cm can bring the tines into the crop protection zone. In AgroSense, open Implement > Offset Calibration, stop the robot over a row, and measure the distance from the outermost tine to the nearest plant stem on both sides. Enter both values and the system recalculates the offset. Maintain a minimum crop clearance of 8 cm for seedlings below 15 cm in height. Re-check the offset after changing the wheel track or remounting any implement.

title: Troubleshooting One-Time Password Delivery Failures at Login
text: AgroSense authenticates users with a six-digit one-time password (OTP) sent by SMS to the registered mobile number. The OTP is valid for 5 minutes, and a new code can be requested after a 60-second cooldown, up to 5 requests per hour; further attempts return error AS-401 and lock OTP requests for 30 minutes. If no SMS arrives, confirm that Do Not Disturb (DND) blocking of service messages is disabled, that the SIM has signal, and that the number matches the one registered on the account. After the second failed attempt, users may select 'Receive code via voice call'. If the registered number has changed, the FPO administrator must update it under Settings > Profile > Mobile Number, or the user must contact support with photo identification.

title: Creating a Field Boundary by Perimeter Walk
text: Field boundaries can be recorded by walking the perimeter with the AgroSense app or the HawkRC controller. Open Fields > New Field > Walk Boundary, stand at a corner, and tap Start. The app records a vertex every 2 metres; tap Add Corner at each turn for sharper geometry. Phone GPS typically achieves 2 to 5 metre accuracy, whereas a HawkRC connected to a PinPoint B1 base station achieves approximately 2 centimetres. Close the loop within 3 metres of the starting point, then tap Finish. Boundaries with fewer than 4 vertices or with self-intersecting edges are rejected with error AS-212. For spray missions, Halcyon recommends RTK-walked boundaries to prevent overspray onto neighbouring plots.

title: Importing Field Boundaries from KML and Shapefile Formats
text: Existing boundary data can be imported through the AgroSense web portal under Fields > Import, available on Pro and FPO/Enterprise plans. Supported formats are KML, KMZ, GeoJSON and ESRI Shapefile; shapefiles must be uploaded as a single ZIP archive containing the .shp, .shx, .dbf and .prj files. The maximum upload size is 20 MB, with up to 500 polygons per file. Coordinates must be in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) or in a projection declared in the .prj file; files without a projection are rejected with error AS-215. Polygon names are taken from the 'Name' attribute where present. Imported boundaries appear in the mobile app after the next sync. Import from the Android app is limited to KML files under 5 MB.

title: Configuring Swath Width and Overlap in Mission Planning
text: In AgroSense mission planning (Missions > New > Spray Settings), the swath width defines the lateral distance between adjacent flight passes. Default values are 4.5 metres for the FieldHawk F2 and 6.5 metres for the FieldHawk F3 at a flight height of 2.5 metres above the canopy. The overlap setting, adjustable from 0 to 30 per cent with a default of 10 per cent, reduces the spacing between passes to compensate for drift. Visible unsprayed strips between passes indicate that the swath is too wide or the overlap too low; strips of excess application indicate the opposite. Changing flight height automatically recalculates the recommended swath. The headland margin, a buffer kept inside the boundary, defaults to 1 metre.

title: Resolving Data Conflicts After Offline Field Sessions
text: AgroSense supports offline operation for up to 7 days. Missions, spray logs and boundary edits made without connectivity are stored locally and uploaded automatically when the device reconnects. A sync conflict occurs when the same field or mission was modified on two devices, or on a device and the web portal, before synchronisation. Conflicted records are flagged with a yellow warning icon and error AS-409. To resolve, open Sync > Conflicts, compare the local and server versions side by side, and select Keep Local, Keep Server, or Keep Both, which saves a copy. Spray logs are never overwritten; both versions are retained. Unsynced data older than 7 days is preserved on the device but must be uploaded manually via Sync > Force Upload.

title: Exporting Spray Records for Regulatory and Subsidy Documentation
text: Spray application records can be exported from Reports > Spray Logs on the AgroSense web portal. Select a date range, fields and aircraft, then choose PDF (Signed Summary) or CSV. Each record includes date, start and end time, GPS track, area treated in hectares, product name, dose per hectare, total volume, pilot name and certificate number, and aircraft serial number. The PDF summary carries a digital signature and a QR verification code accepted by state agriculture departments for drone subsidy claims under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation. Each export covers a maximum of 12 months. Basic plan users can export only the last 30 days; Pro and FPO/Enterprise plans retain spray logs for 5 years.

title: Interpreting NDVI Colour Scales in Crop Health Maps
text: AgroSense NDVI maps display the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index on a scale from -1 to +1. Dark green (0.6 and above) indicates dense, healthy vegetation; light green (0.4 to 0.6) indicates moderate vigour; yellow (0.2 to 0.4) indicates stressed or sparse vegetation; orange and red (below 0.2) indicate bare soil, severe stress or dead plants; blue indicates standing water. Values depend on crop stage, so fields early in the season naturally appear yellow. Compare maps of the same field over time rather than across different crops. Low-vigour zones should be verified on the ground before treatment, because shadows, weeds and irrigation can distort readings. The legend can be switched to the Relative scale under Map > NDVI > Legend to stretch contrast within a single field.

title: Imagery Requirements for NDVI Map Generation
text: NDVI processing requires imagery containing both near-infrared (NIR) and red bands. Standard RGB photographs from the FieldHawk navigation camera or a smartphone do not contain a NIR band and cannot produce NDVI; uploading such images returns error AS-322, 'Missing NIR band'. Supported sources are the Halcyon MS-5 multispectral camera payload, compatible third-party multispectral sensors delivering GeoTIFF files, and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, available to Pro and FPO/Enterprise subscribers at 10-metre resolution with a revisit interval of about 5 days. Satellite NDVI is not generated on days when cloud cover exceeds 40 per cent. For RGB-only imagery, AgroSense offers the VARI index as an alternative, although it is less reliable for detecting crop stress.

title: Managing User Roles and Permissions in FPO Accounts
text: FPO/Enterprise accounts support multiple users with role-based access, configured under Settings > Fleet > Roles. Four roles are available. Owner has full control, including billing and account deletion, and is limited to one per account. Administrator manages users, aircraft, robots and fields. Pilot may plan and fly missions and view spray logs for assigned fields only. Viewer has read-only access to maps and reports. Invitations are sent by SMS and expire after 72 hours. A Pilot cannot arm an aircraft that is not assigned to them; such attempts return error AS-403. Removing a user immediately revokes access on all devices, while their historical spray logs remain attributed to them. FPO plans include 10 user seats; additional seats cost INR 499 per user per year.

title: Recovering from Interrupted Over-the-Air Firmware Updates
text: Over-the-air (OTA) HawkOS updates are delivered through AgroSense under Fleet > Device > Firmware. Before starting, ensure the aircraft battery is above 50 per cent, the HawkRC above 40 per cent, and the phone on a stable Wi-Fi or 4G connection; the package is approximately 180 MB. If the update is interrupted, the flight controller enters recovery mode, indicated by alternating red and yellow status lights, and AgroSense reports error AS-517. Do not power off the aircraft. Reconnect and select Retry Update; the device retains the previous firmware in a backup partition, so it cannot be permanently disabled by a failed update. If three retries fail, connect the aircraft to a computer by USB-C and run HawkFlash Recovery Tool version 2.1 or later.

title: Minimum Android Requirements and Crashes on Older Devices
text: The AgroSense Android app version 5.x requires Android 9 (API level 28) or later, at least 3 GB of RAM, and 2 GB of free storage. On devices running Android 7 or 8, the app may close unexpectedly at launch or when opening the map; these versions are unsupported from 31 March 2026. Users on unsupported devices can install the legacy app AgroSense Lite version 4.8, which supports viewing fields and logs but not mission planning or flight control. If crashes occur on a supported device, clear the app cache under Android Settings > Apps > AgroSense > Storage, update Android System WebView, and reinstall the app. Crash reports can be submitted from Help > Report Problem.

title: Resolving Blank or Grey Satellite Map Tiles
text: When the AgroSense map shows grey squares or a blank background instead of satellite imagery, the base map tiles have failed to load. Common causes are a connection slower than 1 Mbps, a full tile cache, zoom levels beyond 19 where high-resolution imagery is unavailable in many rural areas, or an imagery provider outage reported as error AS-503. First, switch the base layer under Map > Layers between Satellite HD and Satellite Standard. Next, clear cached tiles under Settings > Storage > Map Cache; the cache is limited to 1.5 GB. Field boundaries remain visible on a plain grid without imagery, and missions can still be flown. Current provider status is published at status.agrosense.in.

title: Discrepancies Between Mapped Area and Land Revenue Records
text: Field area calculated by AgroSense may differ from figures in land revenue records such as the 7/12 extract. Typical causes include boundary accuracy, since phone GPS can introduce 3 to 8 per cent error on small plots; bunds and field margins excluded from the mapped polygon; outdated survey records; and unit conversion. AgroSense uses the following conversions: 1 hectare equals 2.471 acres, and 1 acre equals 40 guntha. Bigha values vary by state and are configured under Settings > Units > Local Units. For billing of custom-hiring services, Halcyon recommends using the treated area recorded in the spray log rather than the record area. AgroSense measurements are indicative only and are not valid for legal survey, boundary disputes or land-title purposes.

title: AgroSense Subscription Plans and Pricing
text: AgroSense is offered in three plans. Basic is free and supports one aircraft, up to 25 fields, manual mission planning and 30 days of log history. Pro costs INR 6,999 per year per account and adds unlimited fields, satellite NDVI, boundary file import, terrain-following missions and 5-year log retention. FPO/Enterprise costs INR 24,999 per year and includes 10 user seats, fleet management for up to 20 machines, role-based permissions, API access and priority support. All prices exclude 18 per cent GST. A 30-day Pro trial is available once per account. Plans can be upgraded at any time with pro-rated billing under Settings > Subscription; downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing cycle.

title: Halcyon Care Warranty Coverage Periods by Product
text: The Halcyon Care standard warranty covers manufacturing defects from the date of invoice. FieldHawk F2 and F3 airframes, motors and flight controllers are covered for 12 months or 300 flight hours, whichever occurs first. PowerCell 22 and PowerCell 30 batteries are covered for 6 months or 300 charge cycles. The ChargeHub 4 and HawkRC are covered for 12 months. The PinPoint B1 base station is covered for 24 months. Tiller-X chassis and drive motors are covered for 24 months, and TX-Pack batteries for 12 months. Spray nozzles, propellers and weeder blades are consumables subject to normal wear and are not covered. Halcyon Care Plus extends airframe coverage by 12 months for INR 18,000 if purchased within 30 days of invoice.

title: Conditions That Void Halcyon Care Warranty
text: Warranty coverage is voided for the affected unit in the following cases: physical damage from crashes, collisions or falls; water ingress beyond the rated IP protection, including submersion or cleaning with pressure washers; repair, disassembly or modification by anyone other than a Halcyon-authorised service centre; use of non-Halcyon batteries, chargers or propellers; installation of unofficial firmware; and operation outside published limits for wind speed, payload or temperature. A tampered or removed serial-number label also voids coverage. Flight logs are reviewed during every claim to determine the cause of failure. Accidental damage is not covered under the standard warranty but may be covered by the optional Halcyon Accident Protection plan or by third-party insurance.

title: Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) Procedure
text: To return equipment for repair, raise an RMA request in AgroSense under Help > Service > New RMA or through PartsDesk. Provide the serial number, invoice copy, a description of the fault and photographs; for aircraft, flight logs are attached automatically. An RMA number in the format RMA-YY-NNNNN is issued within 2 working days. Pack the unit in its original case with the RMA number written on the outside, after removing propellers and draining all spray liquid. Batteries must be shipped below 30 per cent charge. Halcyon arranges free pickup within Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh for in-warranty claims; elsewhere, the customer ships the unit to Nashik at their own cost. Repairs proceed only after the customer approves a diagnosis estimate.

title: Locating Service Centres and Expected Turnaround Times
text: Authorised Halcyon service centres operate in Nashik, Pune, Aurangabad, Indore, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Ludhiana. The nearest centre can be found in AgroSense under Help > Service Centres, which sorts locations by distance using the device location and lists the address, working hours and phone number. Centres are open Monday to Saturday, 09:30 to 18:00. Standard turnaround is 5 to 7 working days for drones and 7 to 10 working days for Tiller-X, excluding transit time. Express service with a 48-hour turnaround is available at the Nashik and Pune centres for INR 2,500 per unit. During the monsoon spraying season (June to September), an on-site technician visit can be booked at INR 1,200 per visit plus parts.

title: Ordering Spare Parts Through PartsDesk
text: Genuine spare parts are ordered through PartsDesk, available at parts.halcyonagro.in and within AgroSense under Help > PartsDesk. Search by part number or browse the exploded diagram for each product model to identify components visually. Prices include GST; for example, an F2 propeller pair costs INR 850 and an F3 spray nozzle set costs INR 1,400. Payment is accepted by UPI, card, net banking, or cash on delivery for orders below INR 10,000. Orders placed before 14:00 are dispatched the same working day, with delivery in 2 to 5 working days. FPO accounts can obtain a GST invoice by entering their GSTIN at checkout. Unused parts in original packaging may be returned for a refund within 10 days of delivery.

title: Operator Training and Certification Programme
text: Halcyon conducts a 5-day drone operator course at its Nashik and Indore training centres, covering flight principles, HawkOS and AgroSense operation, chemical handling and emergency procedures. The programme is aligned with DGCA remote pilot certification requirements; candidates must be at least 18 years old and have passed Class 10. The fee is INR 35,000, including accommodation, and one free seat is provided with each FieldHawk purchase. A 1-day Tiller-X operator course costs INR 4,000. Graduates receive a Halcyon Certified Operator ID, which must be entered under Settings > Profile > Certification before a Pilot account can arm an aircraft. Batches start on the first Monday of every month; registration is available under Help > Training.

title: Documentation Required for Insurance Claims After an Incident
text: Following an accident involving a FieldHawk or Tiller-X, insurers typically require the following documents within 15 days: a completed claim form, a copy of the purchase invoice, the policy number, photographs of the damaged unit and the site, and an incident report. AgroSense generates the incident report under Fleet > Device > Incidents > Generate Report, including the flight or drive log, last known position, battery telemetry and error codes recorded in the 60 seconds before the event. For incidents involving third-party injury or property damage, a copy of the police First Information Report (FIR) is also required. Halcyon service centres issue a damage assessment and repair estimate within 3 working days for submission to the insurer.

title: Sharing Field Data with Advisors and Data Privacy Controls
text: Field data, including boundaries, NDVI maps and spray logs, belongs to the account holder. To share data with an agronomist or consultant, open the field and select Share > Invite Advisor, then enter their mobile number or email address. Advisors receive read-only access to the selected fields only, and access can be set to expire after 7, 30 or 90 days, or revoked at any time under Settings > Privacy > Shared Access. Halcyon does not sell personal or field data to third parties. Anonymised, aggregated data may be used to improve products unless the user opts out under Settings > Privacy > Data Usage. Account deletion removes all data within 30 days, except records retained for legal compliance.

title: API Access for Enterprise System Integration
text: FPO/Enterprise subscribers can use the AgroSense REST API to integrate field, mission and spray-log data with ERP, accounting or traceability systems. API keys are generated under Settings > Developer > API Keys, and each key can be scoped to read-only or read-write access. Requests are authenticated with a bearer token and limited to 600 requests per minute per account; exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429. Webhooks can notify external systems when a mission completes or a spray log is finalised. Data is returned in JSON, with geometries in GeoJSON. Full documentation and a sandbox environment are available at developer.agrosense.in. Keys that remain unused for 180 days are revoked automatically.
